correctness.rationale: The arm-natural Lütgehetmann one-dimensional queue-and-center model gives a finite connected graph quotient without edge reversals. For a symmetry with f fixed arms the A/B/edge fixed-cell counts are R_p(f), pR_{p-1}(f), and fpR_{p-1}(f), so Burnside gives the rank exactly. Full symmetric quotient orbit types are multisets of queues, with an extra target arm; these stabilize as combinatorial graphs for m>=p. Falling-factorial moments of fixed points give sharp difference p-1. The executable enumerates 42 independent quotient graphs; no finite test is used as an infinite proof. Risk: requires the standard cube-model deformation to be chosen naturally under arm permutations, supported by the canonical edge-order construction and uniform arm parametrizations.

value.rationale: A natural 2026 program seeks equivariant configuration-space information beyond two particles. The complete all-subgroup orbit-space homotopy classification supplies integral fundamental groups and a uniform Burnside formula. It additionally proves combinatorial (rather than just homological) stabilization at the best possible arm threshold for every number of particles, a meaningful structural strengthening rather than a small numerical table.
